Gilead Sciences has announced a new arm of its HIV Women’s Prevention Study to evaluate the efficacy of the investigational long-acting HIV-1 capsid inhibitor, lenacapavir, in combination with Descovy for PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis). This study aims to explore innovative approaches to HIV prevention in women. 2. The Antibody Society has compiled a list of antibody therapeutics that are either approved or under regulatory review in the European Union or the United States. This resource provides a comprehensive overview of the current landscape of antibody-based treatments. 3. Laustsen AH has discussed the potential of monoclonal antibodies in combating neglected tropical diseases and other infectious diseases. This review highlights the versatility and therapeutic promise of monoclonal antibodies in addressing global health challenges. 4. The FDA has approved a new HIV treatment specifically designed for patients with limited treatment options. This approval represents a significant advancement in addressing the needs of individuals with multidrug-resistant HIV. 5. Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) have shown promise in the treatment and prevention of HIV-1 infection. Cohen YZ and Caskey M have reviewed the potential of these antibodies to revolutionize HIV care by targeting diverse viral strains. 6. Xu L and colleagues have demonstrated that trispecific broadly neutralizing HIV antibodies can mediate potent protection against SHIV (simian-human immunodeficiency virus) in macaques. This preclinical study underscores the potential of engineered antibodies in HIV prevention. 7. Caskey M has further explored the role of broadly neutralizing antibodies in HIV treatment and prevention, emphasizing their ability to suppress viremia and prevent viral acquisition in clinical and preclinical settings. 8. Moldt E and colleagues have shown that highly potent HIV-specific antibodies can neutralize the virus in vitro and provide effective protection against mucosal SHIV challenges in vivo. This study highlights the translational potential of antibody-based therapies. 9. Mayer KH and collaborators have conducted a Phase 1 randomized trial to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunological activity of the anti-HIV monoclonal antibody VRC01 in HIV-uninfected adults. The results support the feasibility of antibody-based prevention strategies. 10. Ledgerwood JE and colleagues have assessed the safety, pharmacokinetics, and neutralization capacity of the broadly neutralizing HIV-1 monoclonal antibody VRC01 in healthy adults. This study provides foundational data for the clinical development of VRC01. 11. Cunningham CK and collaborators have evaluated the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of the broadly neutralizing HIV-1 monoclonal antibody VRC01 in HIV-exposed newborn infants. This research highlights the potential of antibody-based interventions in preventing mother-to-child transmission of HIV. 12. Corey L has presented findings on the use of VRC01 antibodies for HIV prevention at the HIV Research for Prevention (HIV R4P) Virtual Conference. These findings contribute to the growing body of evidence supporting antibody-based prevention strategies. 13. Corey L and colleagues have conducted two randomized trials to assess the efficacy of neutralizing antibodies in preventing HIV-1 acquisition. The results, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, provide critical insights into the potential of antibody-based prevention. 14. Gaudinski MR and collaborators have evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of the Fc-modified HIV-1 monoclonal antibody VRC01LS in a Phase 1 open-label clinical trial involving healthy adults. This study explores the potential of long-acting antibody formulations. 15. Caskey M and colleagues have demonstrated that the broadly neutralizing antibody 3BNC117 can suppress viremia in HIV-1-infected individuals. This research highlights the therapeutic potential of bNAbs in managing HIV infection. 16. Chen G and collaborators have assessed the safety and virologic effects of the broadly neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies VRC01LS and VRC07-523LS in HIV-infected adults during a Phase 1 clinical trial. The findings support the continued development of these antibodies. 17. Caskey M and colleagues have shown that the antibody 10-1074 can suppress viremia in HIV-1-infected individuals. This study underscores the potential of antibody-based therapies in achieving viral suppression. 18. Stephenson KE and collaborators have evaluated the therapeutic activity of the PGT121 monoclonal antibody in HIV-infected adults. This research contributes to the understanding of antibody-based treatment strategies. 19. Zhou P and colleagues have identified HIV-1 strains that exhibit broad resistance to CD4-binding site neutralizing antibodies. This study highlights the challenges of developing effective antibody-based therapies against diverse viral strains. 20. WHO has outlined preferred product characteristics for monoclonal antibodies intended for HIV prevention. These guidelines aim to inform the development and deployment of antibody-based interventions. 21. Sok D and colleagues have demonstrated that recombinant HIV envelope trimers can select for quaternary-dependent antibodies targeting the trimer apex. This research advances the understanding of antibody responses to HIV. 22. Padte N and collaborators have explored the engineering of multispecific antibodies against HIV-1. This study highlights the potential of innovative antibody designs in combating HIV. 23. Kong R and colleagues have shown that combining broadly reactive HIV-1 antibodies targeting major neutralization epitopes can improve neutralization potency and breadth. This research supports the development of combination antibody therapies. 24. Cohen YZ and collaborators have evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity of combining the broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies 3BNC117 and 10-1074 in healthy adults. The findings support the feasibility of combination antibody therapies. 25. Wagh K and colleagues have identified optimal combinations of broadly neutralizing antibodies for the prevention and treatment of HIV-1 clade C infection. This research informs the design of antibody-based interventions. 26. Stephenson KE and collaborators have reviewed the potential of vaccines and broadly neutralizing antibodies for HIV-1 prevention. This review highlights the complementary roles of these approaches in combating HIV. 27. Wagh K and colleagues have explored the potential of conventional and bispecific broadly neutralizing antibodies for preventing HIV-1 subtype A, C, and D infections. This study underscores the versatility of antibody-based strategies. 28. Huang Y and collaborators have engineered bispecific antibodies with exceptional HIV-1-neutralizing activity. This research advances the development of next-generation antibody therapeutics. 29. Cohen M and Corey L have reviewed the potential of broadly neutralizing antibodies to prevent HIV-1 infection. This review emphasizes the promise of antibody-based prevention strategies. 30. UNAIDS has published data highlighting the global impact of effective antiretroviral therapy in stopping the transmission of HIV. This evidence underscores the importance of expanding access to treatment. 31. Brown T and Peerapatanapokin W have discussed the evolving HIV epidemics and the urgent need to refocus prevention efforts on high-risk populations. This review provides insights into targeted prevention strategies. 32. Mishra S and colleagues have analyzed the role of sex work in generalized HIV epidemics and its implications for programmatic interventions. This study challenges assumptions and informs evidence-based programming. 33. UNICEF has published data on adolescent HIV prevention, emphasizing the importance of addressing the unique needs of young people in combating the epidemic. 34. Mittler JE and collaborators have demonstrated the benefits of youth-focused HIV treatment-as-prevention efforts in generalized heterosexual populations using an agent-based simulation model. 35. Alsallaq RA and colleagues have modeled the potential impact and cost of focusing HIV prevention efforts on young women and men in western Kenya. This analysis informs resource allocation for prevention programs. 36. AIDSinfo provides an online database of resources related to HIV prevention, treatment, and care. This platform serves as a valuable tool for healthcare professionals and researchers. 37. Akullian A and collaborators have examined the relationship between sexual partnership age pairings and the risk of HIV acquisition in rural South Africa. This study provides insights into the dynamics of HIV transmission. 38. Shapiro M and colleagues have demonstrated that a single-dose broadly neutralizing antibody cocktail or abbreviated ART post-exposure regimens can achieve tight SHIV control without adaptive immunity. 39. Cunningham CK and collaborators have evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of the monoclonal antibody VRC01-LS in HIV-exposed newborns. This research supports the potential of antibody-based interventions in preventing perinatal HIV transmission. 40. McFarland EJ and colleagues have assessed the safety and pharmacokinetics of the potent anti-HIV monoclonal antibody VRC07-523LS in HIV-exposed infants. This study contributes to the development of pediatric antibody therapies. 41. Hessell JP and collaborators have shown that early short-term treatment with neutralizing human monoclonal antibodies can halt SHIV infection in infant macaques. This research highlights the potential of early intervention strategies. 42. Voronin Y and colleagues have discussed the opportunity to further reduce mother-to-child HIV transmission using monoclonal antibodies. This review emphasizes the potential of antibody-based approaches in achieving elimination targets. 43. Sparrow E and collaborators have reviewed the role of therapeutic antibodies in combating infectious diseases. This review highlights the expanding applications of antibody-based therapies. 44. Brown B and Sugarman J have called for updated ethics guidance to address contemporary challenges in HIV prevention research. This commentary emphasizes the importance of ethical considerations in advancing research. 45. WHO has published guidelines on the quality, safety, and efficacy of biotherapeutic protein products prepared by recombinant DNA technology. These guidelines provide a framework for regulatory evaluation. 46. Sok D and Burton D have reviewed recent progress in the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies to HIV. This review highlights advances in antibody engineering and clinical applications. 47. Morris L and Mkhize NN have discussed the prospects for passive immunity to prevent HIV infection. This review explores the potential of antibody-based prevention strategies. 48. Jain T and collaborators have analyzed the biophysical properties of clinical-stage antibodies, providing insights into their manufacturability and therapeutic potential. 49. Yang Y and collaborators have developed multi-criteria manufacturability indices for ranking high-concentration monoclonal antibody formulations. This research informs the development of scalable antibody production processes. 50. Walther J and collaborators have evaluated the business impact of an integrated continuous biomanufacturing platform for recombinant protein production. This study highlights the economic benefits of innovative manufacturing technologies. 51. Jacquemart R and collaborators have proposed a single-use strategy to enable the manufacturing of affordable biologics. This approach addresses cost barriers to biotherapeutic production. 52. Sahin U and collaborators have reviewed the development of mRNA-based therapeutics, highlighting their potential to create a new class of drugs. This review emphasizes the versatility of mRNA technology. 53. Pardi N and collaborators have demonstrated that nucleoside-modified mRNA encoding broadly neutralizing antibodies can protect humanized mice from HIV-1 challenge. This study highlights the potential of mRNA-based antibody delivery. 54. Kelley B has reviewed the industrialization of monoclonal antibody production technology, discussing the bioprocessing industry's transition to more efficient manufacturing methods. 55. Klutz S and collaborators have conducted a cost evaluation of antibody production processes in different operation modes. This analysis informs decision-making in biomanufacturing. 56. Husain B and Ellerman D have reviewed the expanding boundaries of biotherapeutics with bispecific antibodies. This review highlights the potential of bispecific antibodies in addressing complex diseases. 57. WHO has outlined procedures for assessing the acceptability of vaccines for purchase by United Nations agencies. These guidelines ensure the quality and suitability of vaccines for global health programs. 58. Dias C and collaborators have evaluated the tolerability of high-volume subcutaneous injections of a viscous placebo buffer in healthy subjects. This study informs the development of subcutaneous formulations. 59. Melichar B and collaborators have reviewed the role of subcutaneous trastuzumab in treating HER2-positive breast cancer. This review highlights the benefits of subcutaneous administration in oncology. 60. Bertau C and collaborators have evaluated the impact of viscosity, injection volume, and flow rate on subcutaneous injection tolerance. This study provides insights into optimizing subcutaneous delivery systems.
